thread:
incident-bot: [ALERT] runtime-queueing spike in us-west-2 on inference-runtime. avg_queue_ms=1200ms (>1000ms), p95_latency=1.6s, inflight=94% of capacity. auto-shedding kicked in for low-priority lanes.
maya: I’m on it, paging now. any obvious tenant causing the spike?
alex: seeing a big burst from tenant: search-inc-42, large batched requests around 17:06 UTC. qps jumped x6.
jess: confirming, backend logs show KV cache thrash + long seq lengths on a small subset of requests. this suggests bad prompt pattern causing large tokens.
sam: ok, priority: stop customer errors and keep hosted SLA. proposed live mitigations:
  1) soft-shed low-priority lanes (already active).
  2) temporarily reduce max_inflight for best-effort lane to 6.
  3) bump quota for paying-tenant 'enterprise-phi' to avoid customer impact while we shape traffic.
  4) disable function-calls for non-critical routes (cheap toggle).
maya: +1. I can do the max_inflight and function-calls toggle.
kevin: FYI customer 'enterprise-phi' reported elevated 5xxs, they’re on Slack. If we throttle them they’ll hit us.
alex: plan: reduce best-effort inflight, route enterprise-phi to dedicated slice with quota bump, and set a temporary per-tenant request-size limit of 30k tokens.
ops-bot: runbook snippet: https://runbooks.redwood.io/runtime/queue-spike
ops-bot: suggested command to change inflight:
```
rictl runtime update-slice --region us-west-2 --slice best-effort --max-inflight 6 --reason "inc:1776543210 live mitigation"
```
maya: executing max_inflight change now.
maya: `> rictl runtime update-slice --region us-west-2 --slice best-effort --max-inflight 6` -> ok, rollout started :rocket:
jess: toggling function-calls off for non-critical routes:
```
rictl features set --region us-west-2 --scope non-critical --feature function-calls=false
```
alex: creating a quick quota override for enterprise-phi to avoid customer errors while we investigate:
```
rictl quota override --tenant enterprise-phi --region us-west-2 --burst 5000 --duration 30m
```
kevin: I’ll message their account team and ask them to hold big batch jobs for 30m.
sam: adding an extra shed rule: drop requests with input_tokens > 30k for non-paid lanes.
ops-bot: new traffic shaping rules applied. watching telemetry.
jess: telemetry update in 2m: avg_queue_ms -> 420ms, p95_latency -> 340ms, inflight -> 68%.
maya: much better. still see a handful of long-tail failures (timeout). recommend increasing runtime request timeout from 45s -> 60s for the dedicated slices to avoid mid-request kills until KV cache stabilizes.
alex: agree but do it only for enterprise-phi slice.
maya: done: `rictl route update --tenant enterprise-phi --timeout 60s`
kevin: customer confirms decreased errors, thank you :heart:
sam: next steps: 1) rollback quota bump in 30m unless we need extension, 2) collect sample prompts from search-inc-42 and send to model-onboarding for rate-limiting/heuristic, 3) follow up with a post-incident note summarizing mitigations.
jess: saving relevant traces and exporting cache-miss histogram.
maya: handing off to daytime oncall @alex in 30m for monitoring and follow-up. I’ll attach links to dashboards.
alex: ack. I’ll keep monitoring and coordinate with platform to add a permanent soft-quota for the offending tenant if we see repeated patterns.
ops-bot: incident-bot note: incident resolved -> mitigations stable, no broad SLA breach detected. tag: live-mitigation/runtime-queueing :white_check_mark:
kevin: filed a customer update, shared the temporary measures and ETA for full analysis.
maya: thanks all — adding this to incidents backlog for a root-cause and runbook improvement. :eyes:
